problem_clarity.rationale: The problem statement clearly articulates the gap: high-speed railway embankments on weak soils experience long-term settlement exceeding design tolerances, with no continuous digital twin for real-time comparison of observed vs predicted settlement. The context distinguishes this from static PLAXIS calculations and periodic surveys.

scope_boundedness.rationale: The candidate scope is well-bounded with five concrete in-scope capabilities (data ingestion, 1D Terzaghi model, divergence computation, risk dashboard, shadow-mode operation) and explicit out-of-scope items (2D/3D FEM re-analysis, automated design recalculation, SCADA integration). The shadow-mode constraint keeps regulatory risk manageable.

stakeholder_coverage.rationale: Six stakeholder categories are identified covering the full value chain: geotechnical engineers (end users), RZD (infrastructure owners), construction contractors, regulatory inspectors (Rostekhnadzor), monitoring equipment vendors/integrators, and project owners/developers. This covers primary users, decision-makers, regulators, and ecosystem partners.

assumption_visibility.rationale: Five assumptions are explicitly stated covering data availability (instrumentation), model parameters (PLAXIS extraction), technical feasibility (1D Terzaghi sufficiency for early-warning divergence), regulatory acceptance (shadow-mode advisory), and infrastructure (connectivity). These are the key premises that, if false, would undermine the product.

unknowns_manageability.rationale: Seven unknowns are listed covering instrumentation standards, PLAXIS export format, regulatory requirements for ВСЖД monitoring documentation, data frequency, competitive landscape, deployment model, and relationship to epic 34. Most are resolvable through targeted clarification interviews with RZD engineers and review of Russian railway regulations. However, the relationship to epic 34 is a structural unknown that affects scope definition.

risk_visibility.rationale: Six risks are identified spanning technical (1D model false positives/negatives, instrumentation failures), regulatory (SNiP/GOST non-recognition of shadow outputs), adoption (conservative geotechnical engineers), integration (PLAXIS API limitations), and market (small Russian high-speed rail segment). These cover the major failure modes.

evidence_grounding.rationale: Evidence references are thin: a task description, a previous discovery document (epic 34), and domain knowledge claims. No concrete case studies, regulatory documents, or market data are cited. The proposal itself acknowledges 'no existing GeoSophia codebase or artifacts found' and recommends 'clarify' — indicating evidence gaps that need resolution before formalization.

blocking_gaps.description: Relationship to epic 34 is unresolved — the proposal covers a nearly identical concept for general railway embankments. Without clarifying whether this is a refinement, continuation, or separate initiative, scope boundaries and formalization artifacts may duplicate or conflict with prior work.

Insufficient evidence grounding — the proposal relies on domain knowledge assertions without concrete regulatory references (specific SNiP/GOST codes for ВСЖД settlement monitoring), market sizing data, or case study validation. The 'clarify' recommendation itself signals that key evidence is missing before formalization.

non_blocking_gaps.description: PLAXIS integration path is unspecified — whether parameters are exported via API, manually entered, or extracted from result files affects implementation complexity and error risk. This can be resolved during formalization through technical discovery.

Deployment model (cloud SaaS, on-premise, hybrid edge-cloud) is not determined. Russian railway projects may have data sovereignty requirements favoring on-premise, but this can be clarified during stakeholder interviews.
Competitive landscape in the Russian geotechnical monitoring market is unknown. Existing commercial solutions may set different expectations or already address parts of this scope.

payload.rationale: The proposal presents a well-structured discovery with clear problem statement, bounded scope, identified stakeholders, and honest enumeration of assumptions, unknowns, and risks. The 'clarify' recommendation is appropriate — the core concept (shadow-mode settlement monitoring for ВСЖД) is sound but requires resolution of two blocking gaps before formalization: (1) relationship to epic 34 to avoid duplication, and (2) evidence grounding with concrete regulatory references and market data. The proposal is conditionally ready because the structural quality is high; it needs targeted clarification rather than re-discovery.
